title: Homology consequence of derived Boolean coatom excision
statement: Let $E$ be a finite set with $|E|\geq2$, let $a\in E$, and put $v=E\setminus\{a\}$. For a finite set $F$, let $P_F=\{S\subseteq F:\varnothing\ne S\ne F\}$ ordered by inclusion, and let $B_F=C(P_F;\mathbf Q)$ be its augmented strict-chain complex [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains], with homology as in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For every integer $n$, applying $H^{-n}$ to the derived isomorphism of [lem-sfb-boolean-coatom-excision-derived] and identifying the homology of its explicitly specified suspension gives an isomorphism of rational vector spaces $H_n(B_E)\cong H_{n-1}(B_v)$.

proof.text: Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$. All hypotheses of lem-sfb-boolean-coatom-excision-derived are precisely those of the present statement. Write $f=Q(\check\theta\circ\check p):Q(\check B_E)\to Q(\check B_v)[1]$ for its isomorphism. The cohomology functor $H^{-n}$ specified by the derived-category definition in the statement dependencies sends $f$ and $f^{-1}$ to inverse rational linear maps: functoriality sends their two compositions to the identity maps. Hence $H^{-n}(Q(\check B_E))\cong H^{-n}(Q(\check B_v)[1])$.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category, together with the preceding discussion in Tag 05RR, section-derived-categories; cohomology functors on the localization.

proof.text: The factorization isomorphism DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors identifies the homology of Q applied to a reversed complex with the homology of that reversed complex. Reversal is restriction along the integer shape embedding q ↦ -q. Apply HomologicalComplex.restrictionHomologyIso at q=-n to identify the source with H_n(B_E). For the target, apply the standard derived homology shift isomorphism, (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) 0).shiftIso 1 (-n) (1-n), giving H^{-n}(Q(check B_v)[1]) ≅ H^{1-n}(Q(check B_v)). Apply homologyFunctorFactors and restrictionHomologyIso once more, now at q=1-n, to identify this with H_{n-1}(B_v). These generic isomorphisms incorporate the shift differential sign and apply to every integer degree, including zero terms.

source.place: Tag 010V, section-complexes, definition of chain homology; Tags 011G and 011H, definition-shift-cochain and definition-cohomology-shift. Explicit kernel/image computation for the suspension specified by lem-sfb-boolean-coatom-excision-derived.

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism of step 1 with the source and target identifications of step 2 to obtain $H_n(B_E)\cong H_{n-1}(B_v)$. Its inverse is the composite of the inverse identifications with $H^{-n}(f^{-1})$, so the conclusion is an isomorphism of rational vector spaces for each $n\in\mathbf Z$.
